scope: Theorem 3.1 (Matrix obstruction) of the manuscript “A counterexample to the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-the-Colin-de-Verdiere-chromatic-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 157 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 97677c7a183884f0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every a ∈ (0, 1] there are constants β0(a) > 0 and m0(a) ∈ N with the following property. Let 0 < β ≤ β0(a), let m ≥ m0(a), and let G be an m-vertex graph satisfying the following conditions: (i) Every matching of size at least m/20, partitioned into classes of size at most am, contains two conflicting edges in different classes. (ii) Every matching of size at least βm and every vertex set of size at least βm contain a conflicting edge–point pair. (iii) Every two vertex sets of size at least βm have a cross hole. Then there is s0 = s0(G, a, β) such that, for every integer s ≥ s0, every real symmetric well-signed matrix M for the clique blow-up G[Ks] with exactly one negative eigenvalue satisfies rank M > ms 2 + 1. Consequently µ(G[Ks]) + 1 < ms/2 for all these s.
